key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst, combined with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon-negative scavenger, substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a scalable route to improve photocatalytic carbon conversion by coupling catalyst design with biologically derived co-reactants that also aid CO2 capture.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type HEO: (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6 with layered perovskite/pyrochlore polymorphy.
Used Cs/Ba to raise surface basicity, Bi lone pairs to promote polarization and charge separation, and Nb/Ta octahedra for charge transport.
Compared CO2 conversion under three conditions: HEO alone, conventional photocatalysis, and HEO with microalgae or microplastics as sacrificial agents.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach depends on maintaining stable microalgae-assisted reaction conditions, which may complicate reactor integration, process control, and long-term scalability.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
